column4: Visit note | 2025-12-23 10:00 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Morium Begum, 72, female. Mrs. Begum attends for a review regarding her lipid levels, noting she has a family history where her father had a heart attack at 55 and high cholesterol on a routine test. She works as a farmer, though she also recalls that her elevated cholesterol was originally found in an office health check in Shyamoli. She reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, or dizziness. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L, BP 124/72 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 49 kg. Heart sounds are normal and peripheral pulses are intact. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for lipid management. She was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.
